answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce, slow-earned reputation: like a sonnet, trust must follow a strict form — every completed job adds one verified line, and no shortcut skips the structure. A newcomer arrives in sable anonymity with no history and must earn weight task by task. An attacker cloning a thousand identities faces quartz-hard costs: each fake must pay the full slow price of building a real record, so cloning costs more than it gains.
